title: APX provider registry document
description: The APX provider registry (Part 11 §11.4): every organisation that implements APX, as a server, a data provider, or a client that pushes data. An organisation has one company entry and MAY add product entries, one per product, each naming the company entry as its parent. Add-only: an entry is never deleted or renumbered, only retired. The top-level version increments on every change. Not an APDS UserDefinedCodeList, because an entry carries more than a code.

version.description: Increments by at least one on every change to the file.

providerId.description: A UUID the registrant generates (version 4 recommended), in lowercase canonical form. Permanent: never reused, never reassigned.

parent.description: On a product entry only: the providerId of the company entry this product belongs to. Absent on a company entry. The parent is itself a company entry (it has no parent of its own), and a product entry's namespace equals its parent's.

name.description: The organisation's name, as it trades. On a product entry, the product's name.

namespace.description: The organisation's partner-extension namespace (Part 3 §3.3): extension keys apds-ext:<namespace>:…, endpoints /apx/x/<namespace>/…, topics <namespace>.…, vendor classes <namespace>-<class>. Unique among company entries. A product entry shares its company's namespace: it MUST equal the namespace of its parent. The apx and apds namespaces are reserved.

roles.description: What the organisation does with APX. At least one.

contact.description: An organisational contact: a role mailbox (with or without mailto:) or an https URL. Never a named person.

status.description: active, or retired. A retired entry stays in the file; its providerId and namespace are never reused.

registeredDate.description: The date the registration was merged (YYYY-MM-DD).
